title: Move benchmark-like tests out of the test suite into a separate benchmark run with kept results (after sync lands)
outcome: Move benchmark-like tests out of the test suite into a separate benchmark run with kept results (after sync lands)
acceptance: Tests whose job is to measure time or load (multi-round real-HTTPS workflows, scale phases, wall-clock deadline guards) are inventoried, with each one's current cost on Windows and Linux

Those measurements move to a separate benchmark entry point that is run on demand on a test host such as DL560, not inside the full gate, and that records each run's results durably (host, build, numbers) for comparison over time

The full gate keeps fast tests of the behavior that matters (refusal codes, no-admission, byte and count invariants); no coverage of behavior is lost, and no test in the suite fails merely because a busy machine was slower
Greg's direction is quoted on this item, and Kimi's assessment is recorded

A heavy or load-sensitive test can be quarantined out of the full gate with a reason using Rust's built-in #[ignore = "benchmark: ..."] (no new framework) and later converted into a benchmark case; quarantine never hides a correctness failure, whose behavior check stays as a fast test in the gate

Benchmarks are not a gate: a slower result never blocks a landing, but each benchmark run compares with the previous kept result and any regression beyond a stated threshold is filed as a bug item and fixed
The solution is the simplest useful one (one runner script plus kept results, no heavy benchmark infrastructure), with its cost estimated before building
